question: A particle’s velocity-time graph is a straight line with a negative slope. What does this indicate about the particle’s motion?

options.text: The particle is speeding up in the positive direction.
The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.
The particle is moving with increasing acceleration.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• A velocity-time graph with a **negative slope** indicates that the velocity of the particle is **decreasing over time**.
 
• This decrease in velocity implies that the particle is **slowing down**, provided it is moving in the **positive direction**.
 
• The slope of the velocity-time graph represents the **acceleration**. A negative slope corresponds to a **negative acceleration** (deceleration).
 
• If the particle is initially moving in the positive direction and the velocity magnitude reduces, it signifies that the particle is **slowing down**. Hence, the correct option is identified.
 
• Other options such as the particle being at rest or moving with increasing acceleration are incorrect, as these scenarios would result in different graph characteristics.
